LESSON: SIGN READING 12.4.1 PLAY: CHARACTERISATION

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.4: Sign Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation, part of Strand 12 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Which words or expressions can you use to describe one’s character? 2. Why is characterisatio n important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognize signs of words related to to theme,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. outline the clues for identifying traits of different characters in a play,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. use the clues to describe the characters in a play,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the role of characterisation in determining virtues and vices in the society. • In groups or pairs, learner is guided to observe, fingerspell and sign words related to the theme, • In groups, learners are guided to search from digital and print sources for clues in a play that one can use to identify a character trait, for example; • -what the character does or says; or -what is said about a character, • Individually, learner is guided to brainstorm on the words and phrases used to describe characters and make a phrase book. • In groups, learners are guided to watch signed video clips or sign read sections of a play and identify the clues used to describe the traits of a character 1. Which words or expressions can you use to describe one’s character? 2. Why is characterisatio n important? 153 • In groups, learners are guided to use the clues to assign character traits and display them in a gallery in form of character maps, webbing tools or clusters for peer review. • Individually, learner is guided to play characterisation games that help to summarise traits of all characters. • In groups, learners are guided to dramatize a section of a play to highlight traits of some characters. • Individually, learner is guided to role play different characters in hot seating.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital literacy: the skill of interacting with technology when the learner manipulates digital tools while watching videos on

the sections of a play.

• Critical thinking: analysing skill when learners use clues to assign traits to different characters.

Values:
Responsibility: learners do their part in role playing the characters in a play.

Link to other subjects:

The learner is able to relate the concept of characterisation learnt to role playing in Creative Arts.
